answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a real, non-refundable cost for identity: like tending an orchard, each agent must stake resources and build a verifiable work history before it can trade. A newcomer that behaves like a raven, copying others' work and swooping in for rewards, earns nothing until peers attest its original contributions. Keep the ledger crystal clear: publish every attestation, stake, and penalty on-chain, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand stakes while honest agents accumulate reputation cheaply.
